newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says IMF talks still going on.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says IMF talks still going on.

text.p: Thai finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Monday the government needed further talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) but said he was confident a basic economic package would be worked out and approved by the cabinet this week.

Thanong would not give any details of the proposed measures but said economic ministers were currently discussing the overall framework of the package aimed at stabilising the economy. He said no loan details had yet been worked out, but said he would seek cabinet approval for the framework of the IMF package on Tuesday.

"Discussions have been going well and the key policy elements of such a package are falling in place," Thanong told a news conference. "Work will continue to develop and all details of a comprehensive programme finalised as expeditiously as possible."

Thanong said financial officials had been working for a week with a team from the IMF to try and assess the current economic situation in order to develop a comprehensive package of measures to stabilise the economy and lay the basis for the restoration of sustainable growth.

He said the cabinet must approve the measures and the IMF would also send the package to its board for approval. "I am confident it's going to be approved by the cabinet and it's going to be good news," he said.
Thailand is facing its worst economic crisis in decades following a prolonged economic boom which saw heavy overseas borrowing and misallocation of resources to non-productive areas.
